visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately shows the full sorted array, correct index 7 target, initial mid/high/low and search-space narrowing despite some skipped/overlapped intermediate labels, whereas Lesson 2 mostly displays a single box with mispositioned overlapping low/high/mid markers and lacks a correct array/index visualization for the binary search.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed, wired quiz gate with a real question, plausible options, and a correct answer after act_found, whereas Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning checkpoint.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clear, well-paced narration with spoken math rendered naturally, while Lesson 2 has no narration transcript available, making its audio quality absent and unevaluable.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides timed cues that are mostly aligned with the narrated references, while Lesson 2 has no transcript or cue timing available at all, making its sync impossible to verify and effectively absent.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly traces the binary search steps and explains the halving-to-logarithm idea clearly, with only a minor plan/script inconsistency about linear-search step count, while Lesson 2 provides no available teaching content to verify or learn from.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 is far more polished with consistent styling, readable text, and a structured two-column layout despite some minor label overlaps and a literal \implies artifact, whereas Lesson 2 has tiny illegible elements, severe clipping/off-screen text, overlapping titles/labels, excessive empty space, and multiple broken-looking frames.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents strongly favor Lesson 1 with very high confidence. Lesson 1 has accurate binary search visuals, a functioning quiz checkpoint, clear narration, mostly aligned timing cues, correct conceptual explanation, and substantially better polish. Lesson 2 is consistently described as missing or unusable across key areas: no available narration, cue timing, interactivity, or verifiable teaching content, plus severe visual and layout issues. Minor imperfections in Lesson 1 do not offset its clear superiority.
